name: Solo Whist
description: Solo Whist (or simply 'Solo') is a British trick-taking card game derived from Whist but incorporating bidding elements from Boston and Quadrille. Unlike Partnership Whist, players bid individually to achieve specific goals, such as making 5, 9, or 13 tricks alone ('Solo', 'Abundance', 'Abundance Declared') or losing every trick ('Misere'). It is a game of high skill and nerve.

content.text: Solo Whist (or simply 'Solo') is a British trick-taking card game derived from Whist but incorporating bidding elements from Boston and Quadrille. Unlike Partnership Whist, players bid individually to achieve specific goals, such as making 5, 9, or 13 tricks alone ('Solo', 'Abundance', 'Abundance Declared') or losing every trick ('Misere'). It is a game of high skill and nerve.
Developed in the mid-19th century from Ghent Whist (Belgium). Became wildly popular in British social clubs.
Four players, each ultimately playing for themselves, though they form temporary alliances (one against three or two against two) for each hand.
A standard 52-card pack is used; cards in each suit rank from high to low: A K Q J 10 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2.

Deal 13 cards each in packets of three until four cards remain, then deal the last four singly; the last card (to the dealer) is turned face up to indicate prospective trump. Dealer may pick it up after the first trick if not played.

items.text: Straight Solo: Prop and Cop eliminated; only individual bids (Solo and above) are allowed.
Single round of bidding: Each player has only one opportunity to bid except: dealer's left may Cop after passing if only bid was Prop; a player whose Prop was not accepted may raise to Solo.
